source_explanation:
を is needed because している (is doing) with a color here uses the transitive pattern 'to have a [color]' or 'to display [appearance]'.
きれいな色 (いろ) をしている = 'has a beautiful color / displays a beautiful color'. している here is not an action but an appearance — the fish looks like it has a beautiful color. This is the pattern Noun + を + している meaning 'has [the quality of X] / presents the appearance of X'. Other examples: 丸い形をしている (has a round shape), いい匂いをしている (has a good smell).
Noun + を + している — 'has [quality/appearance]; is characterized by [noun]'

✗ が marks the subject. きれ

でも何でも means 'anything and everything / whatever it may be', used to encourage the student to consult about any topic without limitation.
〜でも何でも is an expression meaning 'anything at all / whatever it is'. 授業のことでも何でも相談してください = 'Please consult me about anything — whether it is about classes or anything else.' でも何でも extends an open invitation, implying there is no limit on what the student can bring up. source_explanation:
次第に (しだいに) means 'gradually / little by little', perfectly describing how the sky cleared over the course of the day.
次第に (しだいに) is an adverb meaning 'gradually, step by step'. The sentence says: 'It was cloudy in the morning, but it gradually cleared, and by the afternoon it was fully clear.' The progression — cloudy → gradually clearing → fully clear — shows a smooth change over time, which is exactly the situation 次第に describes.
